new_statements.quote: It must be emphasized that the vast majority of these languages have not been studied at all, and that proper investigation may result in substantial modification of these generalizations. [...] 2.1.3. Tone. The Mambiloid languages are register tone languages, all appearing to have either three or four tones at the lexical level. The four tone systems are plausibly a development of an earlier three tone system, while the three tone systems constitute an innovation relative to two tone systems found in related languages outside Mambiloid, for example most Bantu languages (Connell 1997a). The different tones, at least in most Mambiloid languages also combine on one syllable to form a number of tone contours.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Group-level only: every Mambiloid language (Luo/Kasabe listed as an extinct member) is a register-tone language with three or four lexical level tones that may combine into contours; tone also grammatical. Nothing on stress/accent; no Kasabe-specific data.
new_statements.exceptions: Author's hedge: most Mambiloid languages unstudied, generalizations provisional. Sister lects documented first-hand have three level tones (Njerep: Connell & Zeitlyn 2000; Cambap: Connell 2002b); Mambila proper has four.
new_statements.identity_note: Family overview of Mambiloid by the linguist who recorded the only Kasabe wordlist (1995). Table One (p.82) lists 'Luo (0)' [speakers], status 'extinct', within the Mambila cluster = Kasabe/luoc1235 (Connell's own earlier name for Kasabe, cf. Iatiku 4). Glottolog files the chapter under Konja-Mambila-Vute [konj1251], not under luoc1235. The tone statement is a GROUP-LEVEL generalization over all Mambiloid languages, not a Kasabe-specific description.

sources.citation: Connell, Bruce. 2016. Lexical Tone in Proto-Mambiloid. Abstract, 2nd International Congress 'Towards Proto-Niger-Congo: Comparison and Reconstruction' (Paris, LLACAN, 2016), book of abstracts p. 15 (footer: '2nd Niger-Congo Congress.. Printed: 28 January 2016').
sources.note: Nothing about Kasabe. Family level only: most Mambiloid languages appear to have four contrastive lexical tones, Nizaa and Vute three, and Mambila lects differ in having three vs four tones; verb roots contrast two tones while nouns contrast three or four; proposes a reconstruction of Proto-Mambiloid lexical tone. No mention of stress or accent anywhere in the abstract.
